name: The HDF Group
subcategory: scientific data format and library (HDF4, HDF5, HSDS)
origin_detail: HDF began in 1987 in the Graphics Foundations Task Force at NCSA, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, supported by NSF grants in 1990 and 1992; NASA chose HDF as the standard format for its Earth Observing System. The HDF Group was created in 2006 as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit (tax exemption August 2006; Champaign, IL) to continue HDF5 development and long-term access to HDF data.
openness_notes: Libraries and tools under a liberal BSD-like licence; developed and governed by the nonprofit itself (17 staff) rather than a multi-stakeholder community, so scored 3.

license_history.note: Date of current licence terms not found

latest_value_type: annual revenue, IRS Form 990, fiscal year ending Dec 2025 (92.6% program services, 0.4% contributions)
risk_events: Revenue has fallen from about $4.6-4.7M a year (2016-2020) to $2.5M (2024) and $3.0M (2025), with deficits in 2024 and 2025; net assets dropped from $2.45M (2023) to $1.62M (2025).
Almost no donation income (contributions $13,149 in 2025) despite HDF5 being embedded in NASA, netCDF-4 and many scientific workflows.
robustness: HDF5 is deeply embedded (NASA EOS data, netCDF-4 is built on HDF5) and openly licensed, so the format would survive the organisation; but the canonical library is maintained by a small staff funded mostly by service contracts.
physical_science_relevance: A core storage format for simulation and instrument data in physics, climate, earth observation and materials science (including synchrotron and microscopy data), and increasingly used for AI/ML data pipelines (the group sells 'HDF5 for AI/ML' services).
openness_effect_assessment: Opening HDF and spinning it out of NCSA created a durable de facto standard, but the nonprofit captures little of the value: 2025 revenue was $3.0M, 93% from paid services, and shrinking. It is a clear case of critical open infrastructure whose users rarely pay for the maintainer.
key_takeaway: The HDF Group shows the 'services nonprofit' model for academic-origin open infrastructure: 20 years independent of NCSA, but revenue has drifted down to about $3M and 17 staff while HDF5 underpins petabytes of science and AI training data. Longevity is real, but financial robustness is thin.
funding_sources: Program services: priority support, training, consulting, data conversion, HDF5 cloud, HDF5 for AI/ML (92.6% of 2025 revenue)
Donations via PayPal and GitHub Sponsors (0.4%)
Historic NSF grants (1990, 1992) and NASA EOS adoption
